description: Drop in a screenshot and convert it to clean code (HTML/Tailwind/React/Vue)

summary.one_liner: A tool that converts screenshots, mockups, Figma designs, and screen recordings into functional front-end code using AI models.
summary.what_it_does: Takes a screenshot, mockup, Figma design, or screen recording and generates code for it using AI models. Supported output stacks named in the README are HTML + Tailwind, HTML + CSS, React + Tailwind, Vue + Tailwind, Bootstrap, and Ionic + Tailwind. It can turn a recording of a website in action into a functional prototype. Model choices include Gemini, GPT, and Claude models, with Replicate used for image generation, background removal, and image editing. When a Gemini key is set, the README says it extracts real logos and images from the screenshot for reuse. The project has a React/Vite frontend and a FastAPI backend, and can be run locally or via Docker Compose. The README also describes a hosted version at screenshottocode.com.
use_cases: Turn a website screenshot into HTML/Tailwind code
Convert a Figma mockup into React or Vue components
Prototype a site from a screen recording
Rebuild an existing page layout as Bootstrap or Ionic code
Generate starting-point front-end code from design comps
how_to_run: Create backend/.env with OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, and REPLICATE_API_KEY (at least one model provider key is required)
poetry install && poetry run playwright install chromium && poetry run uvicorn main:app --reload --port 7001
cd frontend && pnpm install && pnpm dev
Alternatively, from the repo root: echo "OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-key" > .env && docker-compose up -d --build
notable: Supports multiple output stacks: HTML/Tailwind, HTML/CSS, React, Vue, Bootstrap, and Ionic
Accepts screen recordings as input, not just static images
Gemini-based asset extraction reuses real logos and images from the screenshot
Can compare multiple models per generation when several provider keys are configured
Optional screenshot preview lets the agent render its output in headless Chromium and check its work
caveats: Requires API keys from one or more paid model providers; Replicate is needed for image editing and background removal
Running locally needs both a backend and frontend setup; Docker setup does not support live development since file changes do not trigger rebuilds
Ollama open-source model support is described as not recommended due to poor-quality results
Screenshot preview is optional and requires Chromium to be installed
